headline.text: Pregabalin with alcohol showed additive effects on thinking and movement

reported.text: The label describes additive effects on cognitive and gross motor functioning when pregabalin was combined with ethanol, with no clinically important effects on respiration.
The label describes no effect on ethanol and pregabalin pharmacokinetics in healthy subjects.
The EMA pregabalin label states that pregabalin may potentiate the effects of ethanol.

gaps.text: No human studies found on pregabalin ethanol cognitive motor effects in healthy subjects.
searched: pregabalin ethanol cognitive motor healthy subjects

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines or products, like cough syrup or mouthwash, contain alcohol?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Pregabalin and drinking alcohol, change how much this matters?

claims.text: The label states pregabalin with ethanol showed additive effects on cognitive and gross motor functioning.
claims.quote: Multiple oral doses of pregabalin were co-administered with oxycodone, lorazepam, or ethanol. Although no pharmacokinetic interactions were seen, additive effects on cognitive and gross motor functioning were seen when pregabalin was co-administered with these drugs.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote explicitly reports additive cognitive and gross motor effects when pregabalin was co-administered with ethanol, supporting an increased-risk stance for the pair.

claims.text: The label states pregabalin 300 mg twice daily in healthy subjects did not affect ethanol pharmacokinetics and vice versa.
claims.quote: Multiple-dose administration of pregabalin (300 mg twice a day) in healthy subjects had no effect on the rate and extent of ethanol single-dose pharmacokinetics and single-dose administration of ethanol (0.7 g/kg) had no effect on the steady-state pharmacokinetics of pregabalin.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote explicitly reports a measured null pharmacokinetic effect in healthy subjects for pregabalin 300 mg twice daily with ethanol and for ethanol on pregabalin.

claims.text: The label states co-administered pregabalin with ethanol showed no clinically important effects on respiration.
claims.quote: Multiple oral doses of pregabalin were co-administered with oxycodone, lorazepam, or ethanol. Although no pharmacokinetic interactions were seen, additive effects on cognitive and gross motor functioning were seen when pregabalin was co-administered with these drugs. No clinically important effects on respiration were seen.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote explicitly states that co-administration of pregabalin with ethanol was among the combinations showing no clinically important respiratory effects.

claims.text: The review states pregabalin needs further clinical evidence of efficacy, safety and tolerability.
claims.quote: Pregabalin, neurosteroids, tiagabine, and vigabatrin need further clinical evidence of efficacy, safety and tolerability.
claims.judgeRationale: The quote calls for further evidence on pregabalin alone without mentioning alcohol or ethanol co-exposure, so it does not establish uncertainty about the alcohol-pregabalin pair.

claims.text: The EMA pregabalin label states that pregabalin may potentiate the effects of ethanol.
claims.quote: Pregabalin may potentiate the effects of ethanol and lorazepam.
claims.judgeRationale: Independent Claude Opus 5.5 review against the full EMA SmPC section 4.5, supplied in the implementation brief: supports the claim.
